claim: a staff member's role cannot be changed on sv9160: the save requires a Location, and the Location list offers none
_note: fill each proof with: passed true/false, and 'evidence' naming a file, a log line or a measurement. 'passed': true with empty evidence is rejected.

positive_control.evidence: The SAME method -- click a Quasar select, poll for [role=option]/.q-item, click one -- WORKED on the profile menu location picker minutes earlier: options ["Staging Heavy Duty - 9919","Staging Lethbridge - 4310"] were listed and picked, and the header changed (SPECIAL-RESULTS.json C45152, switchedVia.picked=true, locationReallyChanged=true). So the technique can read and drive this app's dropdowns. Also: this very probe proves the method sees option menus when they have content -- it distinguished the staff table behind the dialog from the real q-menu in front of it.

tried_through_the_screen.evidence: Yes -- /administration/staff, the row edit control, the real dialog. The Role dropdown opened and listed all eleven roles, "Time Clock User" was picked and the field showed it (ROLES-UI.json change.picked=true, afterSave.roleFieldNow="Time Clock User"). Save & Close was clicked. The form then displayed "Location is a required field".

waited_and_retried.evidence: Four separate runs (queues gs13, gs14, gs16, gs17), each a fresh sign-in. The last polls for the Location options ten times over twelve seconds. Same outcome each time; the person ended each run verified back on Technician.

checked_for_navigation.evidence: The dialog stayed open after Save (afterSave.dialogStillOpen=true) and the staff list, re-read on a fresh page load, still shows Technician -- so nothing navigated away mid-save and no second tab took the action.

precondition_read_back.evidence: The subject's role was read off the staff list before (Technician), after the attempted change (Technician) and after the restore (Technician) -- ROLES-UI.json subject.roleBefore / roleAfterChange / restore.roleNow.

searched_the_repo.evidence: Rule 97 done: the playbook's §G role recipe was read and followed (it is the source of the Tech role-swap and switch-user routes); its staff ids are staging's and do not exist here. blocker_gate.py's own docstring warns of the script-vs-screen version of this, which is why it was driven through the screen.

asked_what_would_make_this_my_fault.evidence: The likely self-fault was that my selector was missing the option list, as it did TWICE on the other location picker in this app. Ruled out by making the app answer for itself: PROBE-STAFF-LOCATION.json counts the menus on the page BEFORE the click (menusBefore=0) and after (a q-menu with class "limit-select-options" appears), so the list demonstrably OPENED; and its only entry is the app's own message "No results" (afterClick.menus[1].items=["No results"], emptyMessages=["No results"]). The click was a real pointer press at the field's own coordinates, not a scripted .click(). So the emptiness is the product's statement, not my failure to read the list.
